paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshaya, son of Rabbi Shamai.

At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:4, Rabbi Yose bar Bun and Rabbi Yehoshaya, son of Rabbi Shamai, are mentioned: “One said,” etc. Hyman says the name should actually be Rabbi Hoshaya, as in Terumot 3:3: the stroke came off the abbreviation for Rabbi and became attached to Hoshaya.

notes.text: Hyman explains Yehoshaya as arising from the abbreviation stroke of Rabbi attaching to Hoshaya.
